title: Unbounded OpenPGP decompression can kill the client on decrypt
description: A sender can deliver a valid OpenPGP message encrypted to the victim's public key with a highly compressible literal body. The encoded payload can remain below the shared 32 MiB response cap while decompression produces far more data. When the victim taps Decrypt, PgpDecryptor.readLiteral copies the decompressed stream into an unbounded ByteArrayOutputStream before integrity verification and before PgpMimeReader parses it, allowing heap exhaustion and client process termination.
root_cause: PgpDecryptor.readLiteral in app/src/main/java/com/urlxl/mail/pgp/PgpDecryptor.kt does not bound decompressed literal output, allowing a compressed OpenPGP message to amplify into an unbounded heap allocation.
intended_behavior: The client should decrypt a message only within a bounded per-message plaintext budget and return a user-visible size failure for larger content.

trace.description: Reads the authenticated PGP payload body through the shared response-size-limited HTTP client; the limit applies to encoded response bytes.
Passes the server-returned encryptedPayload to PgpDecryptor.decrypt after the user-initiated client-side decrypt flow obtains the payload.
Creates a ByteArrayOutputStream for the decompressed literal and copies the input stream without a maximum output size.
Materializes all decompressed plaintext in memory; a sufficiently amplified valid message can exhaust the app heap and terminate the process.

conditions.description: The victim must open the delivered client-protected message and tap Decrypt.
The attacker must be able to send an OpenPGP message encrypted to a public key accepted for the victim's account.

execution.attacker_perspective: A sender who can address the victim and obtain the victim-recipient public key.
payloads: A valid integrity-protected OpenPGP message containing a highly compressible MIME literal, encrypted to the victim's public key, with encoded size below 32 MiB and expanded size far above the app heap.
instructions: Encrypt and compress a repetitive MIME body to the victim's public key.
Deliver the message through the relay so the app can fetch its client-protected payload.
Cause or wait for the victim to tap Decrypt.
execution.expected_result: The app expands the literal into an unbounded ByteArrayOutputStream and can be killed by heap exhaustion; retrying the message repeats the crash.

remediation.strategy: Bound decompressed literal output inside PgpDecryptor and return a terminal size error before materializing more than the allowed plaintext budget; retain the HTTP cap as a separate encoded-input limit.

code_changes.fixed_code: Replace the unbounded ByteArrayOutputStream/copyTo path with a bounded copy that throws a dedicated size exception once the plaintext budget is exceeded, and map that exception to DecryptResult.Failed/ReadOutcome.TooLarge.

likelihood.reason: A sender needs a recipient public key and the victim must choose Decrypt, but both are normal for the client-protected mail feature and the input can be a valid message.

impact.reason: The result is process termination and loss of client availability for the affected message/session, without data disclosure or account compromise.

confidence.reason: The response cap, decrypt call, unbounded stream copy, and post-copy integrity check are directly present at the cited lines; no parser ambiguity is needed for the resource amplification.
